doc.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: The band as a training ground: Quincy Jones and Milt Buckner
summary: Hampton lists later recruits including Quincy Jones, nearly Ray Charles, and Milt Buckner, then turns to Joe Williams.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So your band was like a training ground for very many young musicians.

Yeah. And later down the line I got Quincy Jones, and I almost had Ray Charles, because Quincy Jones and Ray Charles were doing gigs together in Seattle, Washington. And I got Quincy Jones and he was making arrangements for the band, and then I picked up the piano player, what was his name, oh boy, Milt Buckner. Milt Buckner. You know he plays a lot of kinds of style of piano.
Yeah. He’s a good organist too.
Yeah. A great organist. And let me see here. Oh, Joe Williams?
Joe Williams? There’s a name we like.
